spec.title: Replay S48's delayed setup as one request through the jobs pipeline
spec.description: The third gate of the generic-jobs-pipeline brief, on the real case, run again after one change to what it verifies. VF-076: Spring Boot S48 (example 635, PR #51551) needed the Maven plugin's integration harness, which setup had never exercised, and it took five rounds and six jobs. readiness_gate.py replays it as one request: in a throwaway repository with this checkout's pipeline (jobs/), a consumer job needs the operation in readiness-operation.json, whose base is the S cache made insufficient (without the Maven 3.9.13 distribution and without the ActiveMQ BOM 6.1.8 wherever it is recorded; the operation's base.why says what state that is). The consumer must wait while an unrelated job finishes; one resolution job, admitted by a commit, must fetch what the task asks for from Maven Central, prove the task offline on prepared inputs alone (no network, an empty home and /tmp), and publish a bundle with a receipt that wakes the consumer, whose four WAR readbacks must equal parent.json and fix.json. What is new: the run before this one (20261128-024257, 17 of 17) passed with the home's Maven repository declared under the operation's reads as a bare path, a copy of 770 files that nothing verified. The operation now names that copy by the digest of its tree (6780dd401eda..., 13.1 MB), and jobs/readiness.py reads the folder in full against it before a resolution's first round and before a job is handed the bundle. The gate checks that the operation's digest is the copy's, that the resolution's receipt and the consumer's result both say the folder was verified against it, and, as a fourth control beside the three at the fetch stage (the BOM withheld, a wrong digest for the Maven distribution, a repository that does not answer), that an operation naming another digest for that folder is withheld at the base stage as digest-mismatch before any round runs, with nothing published. 21 checks in all. The folder is thereby verified to be that copy; it is still fetched by no resolution. It runs as one job of the first format, as its earlier runs did; the scheduler under test is the one in the throwaway repository, run without isolation inside this job's limits. It fetches about 9 MB from Maven Central and one POM.
spec.expected: exit 0: every check of the gate passed (readiness-gate.json lists each with what was seen), 21 of 21: the 17 of the run before, the operation's digest for the home's Maven repository equal to the copy's, the resolution and the consumer each having read that folder against it, and the control with another digest withheld at the base stage as digest-mismatch
